prompt: In the Banana card, how are the `h2`, the `p` and the `button` related to each other?

choices.text: They are siblings: children of the same `li`
choices.why: Right. Same parent, one level down from it; that is what siblings means in the tree.

choices.text: Each is the parent of the next one in the list
choices.why: They sit side by side inside the `li`; none of them is inside another.

choices.text: They are attributes of the `li`
choices.why: Attributes are `class`, `id`, `data-testid`; these are child elements.

choices.text: The `button` is a descendant of the `h2`
choices.why: Nothing is inside the `h2` but its text; the button is its sibling.

prompt: `count.mjs` prints the price as `R$ 5,90 <small>`. What does ` ` tell a tester?

choices.text: That the HTML file was written with a typo
choices.why: The file has no price in it; the script's formatter wrote that character into the DOM.

choices.text: A text with an ordinary space describes another string
choices.why: Right. It is the non-breaking space, a different character that looks like a space.

choices.text: The price is not text, so a locator cannot reach it
choices.why: It is a text node like any other; only one character in it differs.

choices.text: Nothing; it is how every space is shown
choices.why: The space before `<small>` printed as an ordinary space; only this one is special.

prompt: A test passes today with the locator `#products > li:nth-child(1)` for the Banana card. What does that prove about the locator?

choices.text: That it is stable, since it found the right card
choices.why: Every candidate reaches the card today; passing says nothing about tomorrow.

choices.text: That the shop will always list the banana first
choices.why: It shows the order today, and promises nothing about the next release.

choices.text: Very little: it matches today
choices.why: Right. What matters is what has to stay true for it to keep matching, here the order.

choices.text: That positions are safer than test ids, which can be removed by developers
choices.why: A position changes with any new card; a test id changes only if somebody removes it on purpose.

prompt: On the shop, in a window wider than 600 pixels, how many elements does the CSS selector `button` match?
hint: A selector does not care whether you can see what it matches.

prompt: `.card small` matches 8 elements and `.card > small` matches 0. Why?

choices.text: The `small` is inside the `p`: a grandchild, not a child
choices.why: Right. `>` wants a direct child; the space accepts any depth.

choices.text: `>` only works between ids and classes, never tags
choices.why: The child combinator works between any two selectors.

choices.text: The `small` elements are hidden at that width, so the stricter form skips them
choices.why: They are visible, and visibility does not change what a CSS selector matches.

choices.text: Playwright counts each `small` once per ancestor in the descendant form
choices.why: There are eight cards and eight `small`s; nothing is counted twice.

prompt: To find the Mango card's heading by the attribute written for tests, the CSS selector is `[data-testid="product-mango"] ___`.
You need the card whose heading says Passion fruit, using CSS alone. What can you write?

choices.text: `.card:has(h2)`
choices.why: Every card has an `h2`, so it matches all eight.

choices.text: No selector; CSS cannot test text
choices.why: Right. A position or a test id can stand in, but no CSS selector compares text.

choices.text: `.card[text="Passion fruit"]`
choices.why: That asks for an attribute called `text`, which no card has.

choices.text: `h2:contains("Passion fruit")`
choices.why: `:contains` is not part of CSS; some old libraries invented it.

prompt: Why does `//p[text()="R$ 5,90"]`, typed with an ordinary space, find nothing although the screen shows that price?

choices.text: XPath cannot compare text that contains a currency symbol like `R$`
choices.why: It compares any text; the trouble is what the text really is.

choices.text: The space is non-breaking, and the text node ends with a space
choices.why: Right. `text()` compares the exact string, and it differs from the typed one in two invisible places.

choices.text: The `p` has no text of its own, only its `small` child
choices.why: It has one text node, `R$`, the non-breaking space, `5,90` and a space, before the `small`.

choices.text: The prices were still loading when it ran, so every `p` was still empty
choices.why: `count.mjs` waits for the list first; the other selectors in that run found cards.

prompt: `//p[contains(., "5,90")]` was meant for the Banana's price and matches 2. What is the danger in using it anyway?

choices.text: None, because the first match is the Banana
choices.why: It is first only because of the order; the expression says nothing about bananas.

choices.text: It is slower than `text()`
choices.why: Speed is not the trouble; matching the Cashew's `R$ 15,90` is.

choices.text: It is right only while no other price contains those characters
choices.why: Right. The Cashew's price already does, and a check could read the wrong card and pass.

choices.text: XPath refuses to run expressions that match more than one
choices.why: XPath returns every match; refusing is what Playwright's strict mode does on an action.

prompt: Match each XPath piece to what it does.

pairs.right: A `button` after this node, same parent
Only the node's own text nodes

prompt: A test uses `#card-4821`, copied from the Elements panel. What happened when it ran?

choices.text: It passed once, then failed on every run after that one
choices.why: It never passed: the run opened a fresh page, which drew a fresh number.

choices.text: It failed on its first run, with `element(s) not found`
choices.why: Right. The id was true only for the page in the browser at the moment somebody looked.

choices.text: It passed, because an id is unique on the page and nothing else shares it
choices.why: Unique on one page, and different on the next load.

choices.text: It failed with a strict mode violation
choices.why: That needs more than one match; this locator matched none.

prompt: After a card for Jabuticaba is put at the top, `#products > li:nth-child(1) h2` fails with expected `Banana`, received `Jabuticaba`. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: The Banana card is broken
choices.why: Nothing changed in the Banana card; the list gained one card above it.

choices.text: The locator found nothing
choices.why: It found exactly one heading, the wrong one, as `received` shows.

choices.text: The locator was testing the order of the list
choices.why: Right. A position leans on the order whether or not the order is what the test is about.

choices.text: The insertion should have waited for the page to load
choices.why: It did wait for the list; the failure is the locator's, not the timing's.

prompt: Why does the lesson call a locator that matches more than you meant worse than one that breaks?

choices.text: It makes the test run more slowly
choices.why: Speed is not the argument; what the test reports is.

choices.text: It can pass on the wrong element, and nobody investigates a green run
choices.why: Right. A false alarm costs an afternoon; a hidden defect costs whatever the defect costs.

choices.text: Playwright cannot report an error for a locator that matches more than one
choices.why: Playwright refuses such locators on actions, which is the protection the lesson describes.

choices.text: It always matches all the elements on the page
choices.why: Two prices, in the lesson's case, not the whole page.

prompt: `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to basket' }).click()` fails with a strict mode violation. What does that mean?

choices.text: The button is not in the page yet when the click is attempted
choices.why: It is there eight times, which is the problem.

choices.text: The locator matched 8, and a click needs one
choices.why: Right. Playwright refuses to pick the first of eight for you.

choices.text: The accessible name was typed with the wrong capital letters in it
choices.why: The name matched; by default it ignores case anyway.

choices.text: Roles are only for headings and lists, so a button has none
choices.why: `button` is the role a `<button>` has by default.

prompt: In the strict mode message, Playwright suggests `locator('#card-9158 > button')` for one of the buttons. Should you paste it into the test?

choices.text: Yes, since Playwright generated it, it is stable
choices.why: The tool only saw this page; the id is drawn again on every load.

choices.text: Yes, but only with `--repeat-each`
choices.why: Repeating runs would make it fail more often, not less.

choices.text: Yes, ids are the fastest locators
choices.why: Speed does not help a locator that finds nothing on the next load.

choices.text: No: it leans on the random id
choices.why: Right. A suggestion is a starting point; this one would fail on the next load.

prompt: `expect(price).toHaveText('R$ 5,90 / dozen')` passed and `expect(await price.textContent()).toBe('R$ 5,90 / dozen')` failed, both typed with an ordinary space. Why?

choices.text: `toHaveText` treats whitespace as one space; `toBe` compares characters
choices.why: Right. The non-breaking space counts as whitespace for the first and as a different character for the second.

choices.text: `textContent` was read before the price was drawn
choices.why: The message shows it received the full price; the strings differ in one character.

choices.text: `toBe` ignores case and compares the words only, so the spaces never count
choices.why: It compares exactly, case included, which is why it saw the difference.

choices.text: The locator matched two prices, the Banana's and the Cashew's, and read the wrong one
choices.why: It was scoped to the Banana card and found one.

prompt: The shop is translated into Portuguese and every button now says *Adicionar à cesta*. Which locators still find the Mango card's button? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: `getByTestId('product-mango').getByRole('button')`
choices.why: Right. Neither the test id nor the role depends on the words.

choices.text: `getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to basket' })` inside the Mango card
choices.why: The accessible name changed with the words.

choices.text: `//li[h2="Mango"]//button`
choices.why: Right. It leans on the heading's word Mango, and the question changed only the buttons.

choices.text: `getByText('Add to basket')`
choices.why: That text is gone from the page.

prompt: Put these locators for the Mango card's button in the lesson's ranking, from the one that lasts best to the one that lasts least.
items: `getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to basket' })`, narrowed to the card
trap: The generated id looks the most precise and is the one that does not survive even the next load.

prompt: A page has a Delete button in each of twenty table rows, and no test ids. A test must delete the row for the customer *Ana*. Which locator follows the lesson?

choices.text: `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' }).first()`
choices.why: `first()` silences the strict check and deletes whichever row is on top.

choices.text: `page.getByRole('row').filter({ hasText: 'Ana' }).getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' })`
choices.why: Right. The row a person would pick, then the button inside it, both by what a person sees.

choices.text: `tr:nth-child(3) button`
choices.why: That is where Ana is today; a new customer sorted above her moves the row.

choices.text: `//button[text()='Delete']`
choices.why: It matches all twenty buttons and says nothing about Ana.

prompt: Before writing a test, what is the cheapest way the lesson gives to check a locator?

choices.text: Run the whole suite and see whether it goes green
choices.why: Green proves it matched today, and a loose locator can be green on the wrong element.

choices.text: Count its matches on the real page
choices.why: Right. With `count.mjs` or the Elements search box: a locator for one thing must find one.

choices.text: Ask a developer which selector they used in the stylesheet
choices.why: A stylesheet's selector is glad to match many; a test needs one.

choices.text: Read the HTML file the server sends
choices.why: The file has an empty list; a test sees the DOM after the script ran.
